notes: Reviewed the actual diff (commit 09c37a4, rentals/frontend/src/app/browse/page.tsx) directly rather than relying on the implementer's summary. The change is a pure client-side state-sequencing fix: a monotonically incrementing requestIdRef is captured at the start of each fetchListings call, and every state-mutating path (success, catch, finally) re-checks requestIdRef.current === requestId before touching listings/total/loading/loadMoreError state. Traced the specific race: a page-2+ 'Load more' request in flight when a filter change fires a new page-1 request (filterStore.setFilter resets page to 1) now gets its result silently discarded on resolution, since its captured requestId no longer matches the ref after the newer request incremented it — no stale append onto the fresh page-1 listings. Also confirmed the finally block's unconditional setLoading(false)/setLoadingMore(false) only fires for the currently-matching (latest) request, so no UI flags get stuck true from a discarded stale request, and no flags get incorrectly cleared out from under a request that's still legitimately in flight. This is a purely local component-state change with no auth, authorization, data-exposure, injection, upload, rate-limiting, or credential-handling surface — it doesn't touch API contract, contactInfo, tokens, or any backend code. No security concerns identified. Note: verification here is code-review only (no LOCAL_RUNTIME_VERIFIED/BROWSER_VERIFIED claim), matching the same environment constraint the implementer hit; that's a QA/runtime-verification concern, not a security one, and doesn't block this review's approval.
